OpsDocument.description: The merged OpenAPI document: the version it declares, its info section, every merged path, the components its fragments declared, and x-fragments naming each source

OpsHealth.description: The liveness response body: a single status field, always ok on a process that can answer.

status.description: The literal the liveness route writes; a live process always answers ok

OpsReadiness.description: The readiness response body, carrying the verdict and, when it is unavailable, one line per part that failed.

failures.description: One line per part that failed; absent when the verdict is ready

status.description: ready when every part answered, unavailable otherwise

get.description: Reads nothing and always answers 200, so any answer at all means the process is up. The route is mounted on the endpoint named by ops.endpoint (default "ops"), which the host assembles unguarded: a probe needs no credential and no tenant.

Serves the document itself rather than a wrapper, merged once at startup and never recomputed, so every request reads the same bytes. Every declared fragment is merged, including those of modules that do not run in this command, because the document states which API this binary provides. Its title, version, description and servers come from ops.title, ops.version, ops.description and ops.servers; it carries top-level openapi, info, servers, paths, components, tags and x-fragments; every operation is tagged with the module that declared it, names its security requirement, and carries an x-endpoint naming the endpoint that serves the route.
get.summary: The API document, merged from every module's fragment

get.description: The verdict is read fresh on every request and nothing is cached or polled in the background: each endpoint the process declared must be accepting requests, and when a database is assembled it is pinged once. Only process-level availability is reported, never tenant or business state. 200 means every check passed; 503 names each part that failed in failures.

503.description: Not ready, naming each part that failed

get.summary: Every declared endpoint accepts requests and the database answers
